topic_map_nodes.title: Mental Model Building
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Mental Model Building - turning complexity into usable understanding
topic_map_nodes.image_description: A human head beside a connected map of landmarks, clear calm composition, exploratory mood.
topic_map_nodes.description: Mental model building is the process of forming a usable internal representation of a complex situation, domain, or system. It supports judgement, planning, explanation, memory, and action by organising scattered facts, relationships, uncertainties, and priorities into a coherent understanding.

topic_map_nodes.title: High-Bandwidth Visual Cognition
topic_map_nodes.long_title: High-Bandwidth Visual Cognition - using vision as a fast channel for thought
topic_map_nodes.image_description: A bright eye scanning a dense but readable map of coloured shapes and paths.
topic_map_nodes.description: High-bandwidth visual cognition is the human capacity to process spatial layout, shape, colour, contrast, scale, motion, and pattern rapidly through sight. It makes diagrams, maps, icons, and visual structure powerful tools for understanding many relationships at once.

topic_map_nodes.title: Semantic Spaces Made Intelligible
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Semantic Spaces Made Intelligible - making high-dimensional meaning readable
topic_map_nodes.image_description: A glowing abstract cloud resolving into a labelled map with paths and regions.
topic_map_nodes.description: Semantic spaces made intelligible are hidden meaning structures transformed into visible, interpretable forms. The concept joins machine-readable embeddings with human-readable maps, labels, regions, icons, and explanations so complex conceptual relationships can be inspected and discussed.

topic_map_nodes.title: Topic Map as Medium
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Topic Map as Medium - a navigable surface for meanings and relations
topic_map_nodes.image_description: A city-like topic map with labelled landmarks, paths, icons, and visible regions.
topic_map_nodes.description: A topic map as medium is a spatial surface where concepts, entities, events, and relationships become landmarks, paths, neighbourhoods, and regions. It supports navigation, comparison, explanation, memory, collaboration, and expressive arrangement of meaning.

topic_map_nodes.title: Semantic Embeddings
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Semantic Embeddings - numerical positions for related meanings
topic_map_nodes.image_description: Glowing points floating in a deep geometric space, connected by faint meaning-lines.
topic_map_nodes.description: Semantic embeddings are numerical vector representations that place texts, topics, images, or concepts near others with related meaning. They enable similarity search, clustering, retrieval, recommendation, projection, topic mapping, and computational treatment of conceptual relationships.

topic_map_nodes.title: Dimensionality Reduction
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Dimensionality Reduction - compressing high-dimensional meaning into a plane
topic_map_nodes.image_description: A many-dimensional wireframe squeezed into a flat labelled map, with visible tension.
topic_map_nodes.description: Dimensionality reduction converts high-dimensional data into two-dimensional or three-dimensional coordinates for display, analysis, or exploration. It reveals visible patterns but also creates distortion because many hidden dimensions must be compressed into a limited visual space.

topic_map_nodes.title: Raw Projection Messiness
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Raw Projection Messiness - why direct 2D maps often become unreadable
topic_map_nodes.image_description: A cramped map of tangled labels and overlapping icons, messy but analytically clear.
topic_map_nodes.description: Raw projection messiness is the unreadable display that often results when high-dimensional semantic data is projected directly into two dimensions. It includes crowding, overlap, unstable orientation, misleading distances, tangled labels, and ambiguous visual groupings.

topic_map_nodes.title: Screen-Space Dimension
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Screen-Space Dimension - giving topics visible size, shape, and area
topic_map_nodes.image_description: Tiny coordinate points expanding into labelled cards, icons, and soft territories.
topic_map_nodes.description: Screen-space dimension is the practical requirement that visible interface objects need width, height, shape, padding, label room, and sometimes territorial area. It converts abstract coordinates into readable nodes, icons, labels, cards, clusters, and regions.

topic_map_nodes.title: Overlap Problem
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Overlap Problem - projected labels and icons colliding on screen
topic_map_nodes.image_description: Several labelled circles and icons colliding in a cramped map region.
topic_map_nodes.description: The overlap problem occurs when projected topics, labels, icons, or cards occupy the same visible area and become hard to read. It arises because mathematical points have no size, while real interface elements need screen space and collision handling.

topic_map_nodes.title: Semantic Integrity
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Semantic Integrity - preserving meaningful proximity in a visual map
topic_map_nodes.image_description: A compass over related topic nodes that remain close while labels stay readable.
topic_map_nodes.description: Semantic integrity is the quality of a visual layout where distance, grouping, and neighbourhood still reflect meaningful conceptual relationships. It prevents readability improvements, aesthetic tidying, or collision removal from destroying the map’s underlying meaning.

topic_map_nodes.title: Force-Directed Layout Risk
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Force-Directed Layout Risk - reducing collisions while distorting meaning
topic_map_nodes.image_description: Repelling magnets pushing topic nodes apart while faint semantic lines stretch.
topic_map_nodes.description: Force-directed layout risk is the danger that simulated node repulsion can improve visual spacing while weakening semantic accuracy. When repelled nodes drift away from meaningful neighbours, the display may become cleaner but less trustworthy as a map of meaning.

topic_map_nodes.title: Semantic-Aware Multi-Stage Layout
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Semantic-Aware Multi-Stage Layout - readable positions constrained by meaning
topic_map_nodes.image_description: A clean constellation of labelled nodes with no collisions, guided by soft semantic lines.
topic_map_nodes.description: Semantic-aware multi-stage layout is a method for producing readable maps by resolving visual collisions while preserving conceptual relationships. It combines projection, overlap removal, semantic constraints, ranking, and stability so the display remains both legible and meaningful.

topic_map_nodes.title: Orientation Stability
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Orientation Stability - keeping regenerated maps aligned over time
topic_map_nodes.image_description: A compass pinning a regenerated topic map so its landmarks remain aligned.
topic_map_nodes.description: Orientation stability is the property that a regenerated map keeps familiar direction, landmarks, and spatial memory across updates. It helps users compare versions, recognise regions, trust continuity, and add or remove topics without losing orientation.

topic_map_nodes.title: Two-Point Rotation Anchor
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Two-Point Rotation Anchor - aligning layout orientation with stable landmarks
topic_map_nodes.image_description: Two pinned landmarks rotating a map into alignment, precise technical diagram.
topic_map_nodes.description: A two-point rotation anchor is a layout alignment technique that uses two stable reference topics to determine map rotation after regeneration. It reduces random orientation changes and preserves visual continuity across stochastic projection or layout runs.

topic_map_nodes.title: Regions Not Points
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Regions Not Points - representing topics as areas with shape and extent
topic_map_nodes.image_description: Map dots expanding into labelled territories with soft boundaries and clear regions.
topic_map_nodes.description: Regions not points is the idea that concepts and categories can occupy visible areas rather than zero-size coordinates. It supports boundaries, territory, membership, overlap, enclosure, influence, and map-like interpretation of conceptual space.

topic_map_nodes.title: Category Boundaries
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Category Boundaries - visible outlines for conceptual grouping
topic_map_nodes.image_description: Soft boxes and outlines surrounding related map nodes, tidy visual grouping.
topic_map_nodes.description: Category boundaries are visible enclosures such as boxes, contours, hulls, borders, or shaded areas that show which items belong together. They make cluster membership legible, separate neighbouring territories, and help viewers read conceptual structure spatially.

topic_map_nodes.title: Voronoi Topic Regions
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Voronoi Topic Regions - partitioning space around nearest topic centres
topic_map_nodes.image_description: An irregular polygon map divided around labelled topic points, crisp geometric mood.
topic_map_nodes.description: Voronoi topic regions divide a map into cells around topic centres, where each position belongs to the nearest centre. They can visualise local territory, neighbourhood influence, screen-space ownership, and approximate conceptual regions around individual topics.

topic_map_nodes.title: Generated Topic Icons
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Generated Topic Icons - visual symbols for individual map concepts
topic_map_nodes.image_description: A grid of small topic icons hovering over labelled map nodes, playful and systematic.
topic_map_nodes.description: Generated topic icons are small topic-specific images created or selected to make abstract or textual concepts recognisable. They improve scanning, memory, emotional tone, visual differentiation, landmark formation, and zoomable navigation when paired with labels and placement.

topic_map_nodes.title: Topics as Recognisable Entities
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Topics as Recognisable Entities - making abstract nodes visually memorable
topic_map_nodes.image_description: Abstract dots transforming into memorable small characters, objects, and landmarks.
topic_map_nodes.description: Topics as recognisable entities are abstract concepts rendered as memorable visual objects through icons, labels, scale, position, and style. This makes a semantic map feel like a navigable environment with landmarks rather than a plain scatterplot.

topic_map_nodes.title: Salience, Rank, Scale, and Opacity
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Salience, Rank, Scale, and Opacity - encoding attention in the display
topic_map_nodes.image_description: Large bright landmark nodes fading into smaller translucent peripheral nodes.
topic_map_nodes.description: Salience, rank, scale, and opacity are visual priority signals that control which topics appear large, bright, faint, foregrounded, or hidden. They encode attention, importance, centrality, context, and zoom level without forcing every priority into one score.

topic_map_nodes.title: Zoomable User Interface
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Zoomable User Interface - multi-scale navigation through information space
topic_map_nodes.image_description: A magnifying lens revealing nested topic layers inside a large visual map.
topic_map_nodes.description: A zoomable user interface is an information space where users move between overview and detail by zooming. It supports landmarks, progressive disclosure, local inspection, nested structure, scale-dependent labels, and navigation through large visual knowledge maps.

topic_map_nodes.title: Progressive Zoom Disclosure
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Progressive Zoom Disclosure - revealing more meaning as scale increases
topic_map_nodes.image_description: A stepped zoom path from a few large landmarks to many smaller labelled nodes.
topic_map_nodes.description: Progressive zoom disclosure reveals information gradually as scale increases. A distant view shows major landmarks and broad structure, while closer views reveal additional topics, labels, icons, edges, examples, regions, and fine-grained semantic detail.

topic_map_nodes.title: Visual-Linguistic Themes
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Visual-Linguistic Themes - recurring meaning patterns in images and words
topic_map_nodes.image_description: Small themed icons and labels forming a coherent visual vocabulary on a map.
topic_map_nodes.description: Visual-linguistic themes are recurring meaning patterns expressed through both words and images, such as food, fire, trade, danger, status, work, or domestic life. They align labels, icons, colour, metaphor, and spatial placement into a coherent visual vocabulary.

topic_map_nodes.title: Abstraction Levels
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Abstraction Levels - choosing how concrete or symbolic each visual element should be
topic_map_nodes.image_description: A staircase from concrete object pictures to simple symbols and labels.
topic_map_nodes.description: Abstraction levels describe how concrete or symbolic a representation is, from realistic image to simplified icon, diagrammatic mark, category label, or abstract symbol. The right level affects recognition speed, nuance, ambiguity, compactness, and zoom suitability.

topic_map_nodes.title: Map as Expressive Interface
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Map as Expressive Interface - using the visual system to compose meaning
topic_map_nodes.image_description: Hands arranging icons and labels on a map as if composing a visual sentence.
topic_map_nodes.description: A map as expressive interface is a visual system used not only to view information but to compose meaning. Selection, grouping, placement, proximity, annotation, and rearrangement become acts of explanation, argument, storytelling, and design.

topic_map_nodes.title: Drag-and-Drop Arrangement
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Drag-and-Drop Arrangement - manually placing images and ideas on a canvas
topic_map_nodes.image_description: Cut-out images, notes, and labels being moved by hand on a digital canvas.
topic_map_nodes.description: Drag-and-drop arrangement is direct manipulation of images, labels, notes, concepts, or fragments on a spatial canvas. It preserves the expressive freedom of paper collage while adding digital search, linking, scaling, recomputation, and editable structure.

topic_map_nodes.title: Reverse Projection
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Reverse Projection - inferring semantic meaning from a chosen map position
topic_map_nodes.image_description: An arrow running from a placed map node back into a glowing high-dimensional cloud.
topic_map_nodes.description: Reverse projection estimates a high-dimensional representation from a chosen low-dimensional map position. It allows manual placement to become a semantic query about what an object would mean relative to existing concepts, examples, and embedding geometry.

topic_map_nodes.title: Moving Things as Thinking
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Moving Things as Thinking - spatial arrangement as cognitive work
topic_map_nodes.image_description: A hand moving symbolic objects while thought lines connect and rearrange.
topic_map_nodes.description: Moving things as thinking is the cognitive practice of using spatial rearrangement to compare, test, refine, and discover relationships. Physically or digitally moving concepts can make implicit associations visible and support reasoning through external structure.

topic_map_nodes.title: Paper-Like Digital Canvas
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Paper-Like Digital Canvas - keeping free spatial arrangement in software
topic_map_nodes.image_description: Paper notes and digital icons sharing a single open canvas, tactile mood.
topic_map_nodes.description: A paper-like digital canvas preserves the freedom of arranging notes, images, sketches, and labels in open space while adding computational affordances. It supports provisional thinking, loose grouping, recomposition, annotation, search, zoom, and structured reuse.

topic_map_nodes.title: Local-Global Layout Tension
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Local-Global Layout Tension - good neighbourhoods can still make a distorted whole
topic_map_nodes.image_description: A tidy local web embedded inside a warped larger net, analytical mood.
topic_map_nodes.description: Local-global layout tension is the trade-off where a projection preserves nearby relationships but distorts the overall shape of a dataset. It matters when a map must support both neighbourhood inspection and reliable interpretation of global conceptual structure.

topic_map_nodes.title: Shared Representational Geometry
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Shared Representational Geometry - meaningful shapes inside learned spaces
topic_map_nodes.image_description: A luminous geometric shape appearing inside several layered representation spaces.
topic_map_nodes.description: Shared representational geometry is the idea that learned systems may contain structured shapes for concepts, sequences, categories, and behaviours. It links semantic maps, embeddings, neural representations, interpretability, transfer, and cross-model comparison.

topic_map_nodes.title: Cross-Model Geometric Patterns
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Cross-Model Geometric Patterns - recurring structures across different models
topic_map_nodes.image_description: Three translucent model spaces with matching shapes highlighted in each one.
topic_map_nodes.description: Cross-model geometric patterns are recurring internal structures found across different trained models. They suggest that independently learned systems may converge on similar representational organisation for meaning, order, category, relation, or behaviour.

topic_map_nodes.title: Cross-Lingual Semantic Shapes
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Cross-Lingual Semantic Shapes - similar meaning structures across languages
topic_map_nodes.image_description: Words from several languages curving into the same glowing geometric shape.
topic_map_nodes.description: Cross-lingual semantic shapes are comparable representational structures for meanings expressed in different languages. They concern shared conceptual geometry beneath different vocabularies, scripts, grammars, translations, cultural contexts, and multilingual communication.

topic_map_nodes.title: Person-Specific Meaning
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Person-Specific Meaning - the same concept carrying different life associations
topic_map_nodes.image_description: Two people seeing the same dining icon surrounded by different associated nodes.
topic_map_nodes.description: Person-specific meaning is the way a concept gains different salience, emotion, memory, context, and association for different individuals. It matters for biographical maps, personal knowledge systems, recommendation, education, and humane comparison of lived experience.

topic_map_nodes.title: Manifold Steering
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Manifold Steering - analysing behaviour through representational geometry
topic_map_nodes.image_description: A curved manifold surface gently shaped by arrows inside a model space.
topic_map_nodes.description: Manifold steering studies structured geometric surfaces inside neural network representations and how movement through those surfaces relates to model behaviour. It treats behaviour as shaped by representation geometry rather than by isolated features alone.

topic_map_nodes.title: Calendar Concept Shapes
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Calendar Concept Shapes - ordered dates and weekdays inside model geometry
topic_map_nodes.image_description: Calendar days arranged around a smooth loop inside a glowing model space.
topic_map_nodes.description: Calendar concept shapes are geometric structures representing ordered temporal ideas such as dates, months, or weekdays inside a model’s internal space. They provide a concrete example of familiar conceptual sequences appearing as learned spatial patterns.

topic_map_nodes.title: Interpretability and AI Safety
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Interpretability and AI Safety - understanding representations to reduce risk
topic_map_nodes.image_description: A shield and magnifying glass over a neural geometry diagram, serious careful mood.
topic_map_nodes.description: Interpretability and AI safety concern understanding what AI systems internally represent, how those representations influence behaviour, and where risks may arise. The goal is to improve reliability, debugging, alignment, oversight, misuse prevention, and responsible deployment.

topic_map_nodes.title: Visual Language Grammar
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Visual Language Grammar - structured meaning from text, image, layout, and symbols
topic_map_nodes.image_description: Letters, icons, arrows, panels, and regions arranged as a clear grammar chart.
topic_map_nodes.description: Visual language grammar is the structured use of text, images, icons, arrows, regions, scale, colour, layout, and abstraction to communicate meaning. It turns visual artefacts into interpretable explanations rather than decorative collections of marks.

topic_map_nodes.title: Robert Horn Visual Language
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Robert Horn Visual Language - historical grounding for text-image communication
topic_map_nodes.image_description: An open visual-language book with diagrams, arrows, labels, and image panels.
topic_map_nodes.description: Robert Horn visual language refers to a body of work on combining words, images, diagrams, symbols, layout, and abstraction into systematic visual communication. It provides historical grounding for information murals, knowledge maps, and text-image explanation.

topic_map_nodes.title: Information Murals and Mess Maps
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Information Murals and Mess Maps - large shared artefacts for complex understanding
topic_map_nodes.image_description: A wall-sized visual map covered with diagrams, notes, images, and connecting lines.
topic_map_nodes.description: Information murals and mess maps are large visual artefacts that combine text, diagrams, categories, timelines, images, evidence, and relationships. They help groups examine complexity, preserve context, surface disagreements, and build shared understanding.

topic_map_nodes.title: Cross-Specialist Collaboration
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Cross-Specialist Collaboration - helping different experts share partial knowledge
topic_map_nodes.image_description: Experts from different fields gathered around a shared visual map with linked notes.
topic_map_nodes.description: Cross-specialist collaboration is the coordination challenge faced by people with different expertise, evidence, vocabulary, incentives, and responsibilities. Visual maps can expose dependencies, gaps, conflicts, shared reference points, and opportunities for synthesis.

topic_map_nodes.title: Pandemic and Biorisk Collaboration
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Pandemic and Biorisk Collaboration - coordinating specialists around shared threat maps
topic_map_nodes.image_description: Specialists around a bio-risk map with virus icons, documents, and connecting lines.
topic_map_nodes.description: Pandemic and biorisk collaboration requires clinicians, modellers, biosecurity specialists, policy experts, communicators, and institutions to share fast-changing knowledge. Visual threat maps can reveal risks, responsibilities, dependencies, uncertainty, and urgent coordination needs.

topic_map_nodes.title: Collective Sensemaking Tools
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Collective Sensemaking Tools - shared media for coordinating understanding
topic_map_nodes.image_description: A group building a shared map together, with paths linking many viewpoints.
topic_map_nodes.description: Collective sensemaking tools help groups build, compare, revise, and act on shared understanding of complex domains. They connect individual mental models with deliberation, education, coordination, disagreement, memory, accountability, and cooperative action.

topic_map_nodes.title: New Media Grammar
topic_map_nodes.long_title: New Media Grammar - emerging conventions for generated, spatial, and interactive media
topic_map_nodes.image_description: A laboratory of icons, maps, generated images, and interface layers forming a new alphabet.
topic_map_nodes.description: New media grammar is the emerging design language of generated images, embeddings, zoomable canvases, dynamic ranking, interactive maps, multimodal symbols, and adaptive interfaces. It extends older diagram traditions into computational and personalised media.

topic_map_nodes.title: Samuel Pepys Life Map
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Samuel Pepys Life Map - biographical topics arranged as historical terrain
topic_map_nodes.image_description: A seventeenth-century diary page unfolding into a labelled city-like topic map.
topic_map_nodes.description: The Samuel Pepys life map is a biographical semantic map of people, places, events, institutions, possessions, illnesses, anxieties, and historical episodes connected with Samuel Pepys. It demonstrates how a life can be arranged as navigable conceptual terrain.

topic_map_nodes.title: Biographical Salience
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Biographical Salience - deciding what matters inside a life map
topic_map_nodes.image_description: A life-map timeline with some personal landmarks glowing brighter than others.
topic_map_nodes.description: Biographical salience is the judgement of what matters inside a life story or personal history. It weighs events, relationships, duties, illnesses, places, emotions, possessions, and historical forces to decide what should appear prominent in a life map.

topic_map_nodes.title: Pepys Medical Anxiety
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Pepys Medical Anxiety - bodily pain as a salient life-map concern
topic_map_nodes.image_description: A dark stone beside old medical instruments and a diary page, anxious mood.
topic_map_nodes.description: Pepys medical anxiety refers to Samuel Pepys’s bladder stone, surgery, cold-triggered pain, bodily fear, and recurring health preoccupation. It is an example of intimate suffering becoming a highly salient concern inside a historical biography.

topic_map_nodes.title: Pepys Work and Institutions
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Pepys Work and Institutions - Navy duties as a semantic neighbourhood
topic_map_nodes.image_description: An anchor, ledgers, and dockside buildings arranged as a tidy topic cluster.
topic_map_nodes.description: Pepys work and institutions refers to Samuel Pepys’s naval administration, official duties, workplace geography, documents, rank, and institutional responsibility. It represents public role and bureaucratic systems within a broader biographical map.

topic_map_nodes.title: Historical Catastrophe Landmark
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Historical Catastrophe Landmark - disaster as an emotionally charged map region
topic_map_nodes.image_description: A burning old city skyline with a cleared space around it on a historical map.
topic_map_nodes.description: A historical catastrophe landmark is a disaster event that becomes a major emotional and spatial anchor in a historical or biographical map. It captures destruction, fear, displacement, civic memory, rebuilding, and the way catastrophe reorganises attention.

topic_map_nodes.title: Prototype First Steps
topic_map_nodes.long_title: Prototype First Steps - early system work with a clear future direction
topic_map_nodes.image_description: A small green shoot growing beside an early topic-map interface.
topic_map_nodes.description: Prototype first steps describe an early but functional system that demonstrates a promising direction while leaving major design, evaluation, interaction, and product questions open. It signals credible progress, incomplete polish, and a path for iterative development.
